content:
sam: heads up — we've been seeing a spike in time-to-first-chunk on streaming gRPC responses when traffic goes through Azure APIM in westeurope. tails are fine after first chunk, but TTFB jumps to ~700-900ms for first chunk.
kevin: any recent edge config rollouts? region-specific?
sam: rolled a tiny APIM policy tweak this morning (header rewrite) at 09:12 UTC but I don't think it should touch body.
marie: can you repro locally with grpcurl or only through APIM?
sam: repro is trivial via APIM. direct to backend (envoy in cluster) is ~60ms TTFB. through APIM -> first chunk ~800ms, then streaming steady.
josh: weird — sounds like APIM is buffering until it sees more data or a flush. do we set content-length anywhere? gRPC uses chunked with http2 DATA frames so shouldn't need buffering.
kevin: capture of tcpdump from pod -> shows TLS handshake fine, HTTP/2 SETTINGS exchange, then long gap before first DATA frame sent from APIM to client. backend already sent DATA frames earlier.
marie: can you paste a short curl/grpcurl example you used?
sam: sure — reproducer: ```grpcurl -proto chat.proto -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H "authorization: Bearer x" -insecure backend.cluster.local:443 ChatService/StreamReply``` when routed via APIM replace host/port with APIM endpoint.
liz: I grep'd APIM logs, there's a bunch of "response buffering" entries for this route starting at 09:10. policy shows `set-body` / `rewrite-uri` earlier today.
kevin: APIM is known to buffer when certain policies are present — particularly if policies manipulate the response or set caching headers. maybe the policy coerces it to buffer the body until the full response is available.
josh: but why only first chunk? If APIM decides to stream afterwards shouldn't it forward early frames as they arrive? perhaps it waits for first N bytes then switches to chunked streaming.
marie: also check http2 SETTINGS like initial_window_size and max_frame_size on gateway vs backend. if APIM advertises tiny window, envoy might stall until it increments.
sam: we captured SPDY/HTTP2 settings. APIM advertises SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=65535 (default). backend had 65536 as well. window seems normal.
kevin: what about Nagle/TCP_NODELAY behavior — are we terminating TLS at APIM then opening new TLS to client, maybe delayed flush?
josh: I tried forcing TCP_NODELAY on outbound from envoy, no change.
liz: deploy-bot: we did a policy rollback at 09:38 UTC for that route.
ingress-bot: rollback of policy 'rewrite-analytics' completed for route /v1/chat at 09:38:12 UTC (change id: ch_2026-04-11-0912).
marie: after rollback any improvement?
sam: after rollback TTFB dropped back to ~80ms. looks like policy was the trigger.
kevin: ok good root cause candidate. what in the policy causes buffering? set-body? transform? even adding any response header modifications can force full-body read in some gateways.
josh: note for APIM: policies that reference context.Response.Body or use <rewrite-uri> may switch into buffer mode. we should audit the policy for such statements.
liz: I pulled the policy diff — we added an analytics enrichment step that appends a small JSON to the response meta via <set-body> if header X-collect present. that probably forced buffering.
kevin: two takeaways: 1) avoid set-body and full-body policies on streaming endpoints; 2) add a lint in our Terraform that forbids response-body policies on streaming routes.
marie: can we implement an APIM-side streaming-safe policy that sets headers only (no body rewrite) and use that for chat routes?
sam: yes we can send analytics events to an async collector instead of injecting into response.
josh: also add e2e test that runs grpc streaming through APIM and asserts TTFB < 200ms. we should catch regressions.
liz: created ticket INF-4234: audit APIM policies for streaming routes and add Terraform lint.
kevin: also add a note in runbook: if chat route TTFB spikes, check APIM policy and recent config changes before looking at envoy.
sam: thanks all — rolling forward with policy rollback as hotfix, and adding lint+test. will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
kevin: nice catch. :clap:
marie: small doc snippet for infra playbook: "APIM may buffer responses when policies touch response body — avoid on gRPC streaming endpoints; prefer header-only or async telemetry."
sam: adding that to runbook now.
deploy-bot: hotfix rollout started for env=prod, change=ch_2026-04-11-0912-rollback, started at 09:45 UTC.
ingress-bot: hotfix finished at 09:52 UTC, traffic green. metrics show TTFB 95th dropping from 820ms -> 110ms for route /v1/chat.
sam: closing for now, will reopen if we see recurrence.
